title: Pathfinder
summary: Self-assessment article: pick one of six experience levels and follow a 'Start Here' link to the recommended entry point in the course. The suggestions are optional.

concepts.heading: Six profiles and where each should start
points: 1. Total beginner: start at the very beginning and skip nothing, because each module builds on the previous one. Get comfortable with each module before moving on; about one week per module is the suggested pace. Start link goes to lecture 37348056.
2. Some HTML/CSS already: begin at the intermediate tutorials and do every challenge. If the challenges feel too hard, drop back to the earlier lessons. Start link goes to lecture 37350296.
3. Under 6 months of JavaScript/web experience: skip the intro programming modules (dip in only if needed) and complete every lecture with 'challenge' in its title to confirm you can skip the rest.

4. Experienced programmer, new to web: usually knows some HTML/CSS, so start at the JavaScript modules. Expect JavaScript to have quirks that surprise people coming from stricter languages such as Swift.
5. Experienced web developer: jump to the back end, starting with Node, then Express, EJS, Postgres and so on.
6. Experienced web developer who only wants React: go straight to the 8-hour React module aimed at experienced developers (link goes to lecture 17038306).
These are recommendations only; learners can browse the curriculum and choose their own route.

pitfalls: Beginners jumping ahead to the 'cool' later modules without the foundations, then getting lost.
